purpose: A template for noting the quantities a rule leaves open and the decisions changed after the values were seen, with the reason, the alternatives tried and the images that used each one, filled in for works 1 and 2 as the worked example (the only record of decisions in the main text). It is the table readers copy for their own series.

row_rule: the main text shows only the rows that bear on its claims (decision of the researcher, 2026-10-29, on the word count, replacing the rule of version 3): the two sides of each comparison whose effect the paper reports (work 1: the height scale, whose alternative is the per-tile min-max, and the drawing; work 2: map B and the percentiles) and one decision of interpretation (the subject of work 2, under the band 'Record of the paper' because it is a decision about what the paper claims and not a quantity of the works); every other decision of works 1 and 2 is in the full table of supplement S1, with the longer wording
acted_on_labels: in the repository the column holds the image files; the numbers of the figures of the paper are put in when the manuscript is made, outside the repository

layout.empty_template: the same table with the six headers and three empty rows is drawn below it
layout.row_order: a band 'Work 1' and its rows, a band 'Work 2' and its rows, then a band 'Record of the paper' and its row, each in the order of the conditions
layout.reason_format: '{why}. Tried: {a}; {b}.' or '{why}. Tried: none.', with the first letter of why in upper case
layout.print: drawn in one grey channel (mode L) on white, with no colour; every font size is at least 7 pt at the printed width
layout.legend: under the filled table, one line: the meaning of the dagger, after its mark

outputs: results/decision_note_v5/decision_note.png, decision_note.md (the same table as text) and decision_note.json (the values read, the SHA-256 of the conditions, the counts of words); results/decision_note (version 2) and results/decision_note_v4 are kept
words: the words drawn are counted as whitespace-separated tokens of the text of each cell, the headers, the band labels, the legend and the titles, for the filled and the empty table; a path of an image is one word and a mark standing alone (* or †) is also one word; the counts are recorded and enter the word count of the outline (the template of the journal counts tables and charts); the run stops if the two tables together exceed max_words
not_claimed: A way of noting decisions; it does not show that noting them helps a reader (no study with people). Disclosure helps a reader repeat the work but does not by itself settle whether a reading is valid or a choice biased. The column of who judged names the judgement made, not the viewers of the paper; 'none recorded' means no look was judged with a sheet, not that the makers did not look. The five rows are chosen by the rule above, not as the decisions that mattered most. The reasons are the makers' statements as recorded in the decision table; they are not checked against a file and do not show that a choice was right. The judged cells of work 2 speak of the row of the 20 words only (the other rows of the blind judgement are in S1); they were judged on the images of the judgement (80 px tiles under five common seeds), not on figure 6 itself. The share used is a record of the 40 words of two trial authors, not a property of the map or of the lexicon; using more of a range is not claimed to be better.
checks: every file named exists and is the one at HEAD; every key read exists; every must_contain string occurs in the keys named (else the run stops)
every image of compared is one of acted_on of its row; the judged of each row is a non-empty literal, checked where a check is given; exactly the rows with dagger true carry the mark
every row has a reason with a non-empty why and a list tried of non-empty strings (possibly empty)
2 rows of work 1, 2 of work 2 and 1 of the record of the paper (asserted as constants), and 6 columns
the saved image, opened again, is mode L at the width of the layout and its dpi, the font drawn (after rounding to pixels) is at least 7 pt, and the legend is one line
the words of the two tables together are at most max_words
the share used of each quantity named in used_range, computed by used_range_rule, matches the string shown, and the literal contains it and the number of words
the outcome of every judged row with answers, computed by answers_rule from the two lists, is the one written, and the literal contains its phrase and the phrase of the row
no cell text before marking contains a reserved mark (reserved_marks)

dagger.meaning: claim weakened in the paper after the values were seen

used_range_rule: the range of a quantity is the one the rule can give, read from atact.mapping (f in [F0, F0 + F1], s in [S0, S0 + S1], the ends of p and q in [0, 1]); its share used is (the largest minus the smallest value of the 40 words of the two trial authors, pooled, the key pooled.<version>.<quantity> of the record) divided by that range, in percent; 'N%' means every quantity named rounds to N, 'over N%' that every one is above N; the literal must contain the string shown and '<words> words', and the words per author of the record must sum to words. The smallest to the largest is sensitive to an outlier; the quartiles are in S1
answers_rule: the judged literal of a row of work 2 covers one version and one row of the blind judgement, named by the phrase of the row: the row remains for a judge if it is in the list of that version (main: the deciding judge of score.json, called the main judge in the paper, whose decided must be true; also: the researcher, of the supplement, whose controls must pass); the outcome is 'both differ' if both lists hold the row, 'neither' if none does and 'split' otherwise; the run stops unless the outcome is the one written and the literal contains its phrase and the phrase of the row. The other rows and versions are in S1
reserved_marks: the dagger and the mark of the compared images are drawn only by the script: a row whose quantity, value, reason, image paths, when or judged contains † or * stops the run
